info.title: JARVIS X
info.description: Autonomous personal operations platform. Observes commitments, predicts failure, prepares the next best action, executes through policy-controlled tools, verifies the result, and escalates only when authorized.

get.description:
Liveness. Deliberately touches nothing — a dependency outage is not a reason to
restart this process.
Readiness. Checks the one dependency without which nothing works.

Render the sign-in form after validating the request.

Validation happens *before* rendering so an invalid client or unregistered
redirect_uri never reaches a page that collects a password.

post.description:
Show exactly what an action would do, without doing it.

The returned ``payload_hash`` is the hash a real execution binds to, which makes
"flip SIMULATE to EXECUTE on the same plan" a checkable claim.

post.description:
The kill switch.

Cancels queued work and revokes sessions. It never deletes evidence — it records who
invoked it and why (blueprint §9).

post.description:
Telegram update ingress.

Telegram echoes a secret we set on ``setWebhook``; comparing it is what distinguishes
a real update from anyone who found the URL. Always 200: a non-200 makes Telegram
retry, and retrying a hostile request helps nobody.

Where Google sends the user back.

Unauthenticated by necessity — the browser arrives here from Google, not from the app —
so ``state`` is the only proof of who started the flow.

post.description:
Disconnect, and by default delete what was stored.

Deleting is the default rather than an extra step: a connector that keeps your mail
after you disconnect it has not really been disconnected.
